## My correction was itself wrong — and this ticket is now OBSOLETE

Two retractions, then the disposition.

### 1. `--caused-by` IS in the rendered help now

My previous comment asserted it was 'absent from that file entirely — from both the usage and the
body'. Checked against current `origin/main`:

```
2:                        [--class CLOSE_CLASS] [--caused-by CAUSED_BY]
19:  --caused-by CAUSED_BY
20:                        ticket that caused this bug
```

My earlier reading of 0 hits was accurate **when I ran it**. The file changed between that check and
my correction, and I re-asserted a stale observation as a current fact — the same error I have made
repeatedly today, one layer down: reasoning from a source without confirming it was still the
source.

### 2. The within-file drift I 'refuted' was reported against a different file

I dismissed the previous comment's finding by quoting a 22-line artifact and noting its usage block
wraps. That agent was reading an **11-line hand-written file** from a checkout pinned at
`8fa8f36b64`; the 22-line generated artifact exists only on `origin/main`. Its observation was
correct for the tree it held. Neither of us was misreading wrapped output — we were reading
different files, and I diagnosed its error confidently and wrongly.

The right lesson, as it put it: *'confirm which tree you're reading before drawing conclusions from
it'* — one `git log -1` against the path.

### 3. The premise is gone: RP-05 S2d removed the second source

`scripts/gen_cli_help.py` now RENDERS `_cli/help/*.txt` from the route registry's parser factories:

> 'Historically those files were hand-captured; this generator makes them DERIVED — one artifact per
> help-backed route in the immutable route registry, rendered by resolving that route's
> `parser_factory` and formatting its `--help`.'

So `build_transition` is the sole authority and a parser-registered flag **cannot** fail to appear.
`gen_cli_help.py --check` fails on stale, missing or stray artifacts, and
`tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py` mutation-checks it — `test_check_detects_a_stale_artifact`,
`_a_missing_artifact`, `_a_stray_artifact`. It rides in the unit suite rather than a CI-only step,
so `project.portability` is satisfied.

That is this ticket's acceptance criteria delivered in full, including AC2's requirement to fix the
duplication **at the root** rather than copy the line across, and AC3's parser-derived test.

### Disposition: obsolete, not fixed

Filed 17:00:02; RP-05 S2d landed the same day. Valid when written, overtaken by in-flight work — the
premise disappeared rather than the ticket being worked. Closing `obsolete` rather than letting a
resolved ticket sit open at P2 (a priority I raised on evidence that was real at the time: two
agents independently misled by the then-missing line).

Both agents that hit this were misled by a genuine defect. It is simply already gone.
